title: Gated API matrix
blurb: Configurable launchQueue consumer that runs activation-gated APIs (window.open, requestFullscreen, showOpenFilePicker, navigator.share) in selectable order and logs isActive before and after each call.
question: How many activation-gated API calls can succeed from a single transient user activation delivered to launchQueue.setConsumer(), and how does call order change which API succeeds?
result: On headed Chrome for Testing 153 under xvfb with popup blocking enabled, click baselines confirmed single-activation consumption: window.open() then requestFullscreen() gave 1 allowed / 1 TypeError, reversed order gave fullscreen allowed / window.open null, and expired activation blocked both. Installed-app launch delivery not verified in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Headed Chrome for Testing 153 under xvfb (click and expired baselines verified); installed-app delivery not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: One focus-existing launch grants only one transient activation, so the first activation-consuming call blocks any subsequent gated call
friction.repro: Enable both window.open() and requestFullscreen() in the matrix and run from a single activation; whichever runs first consumes activation (isActive drops to false) and the second fails.
friction.workaround: Budget at most one activation-consuming API call per launch delivery and fall back to an in-app button when a second gated action is needed.
